reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis is physically sound, correctly linking slower cation diffusion and stable oxide formation (Al2O3, SiO2) to protective scales, and faster Mn diffusion to volatile/poorly adherent oxides, though it slightly oversimplifies the role of Cr and the complex thermodynamics in multi-principal element alloys.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is clear and feasible, with a well-defined falsification criterion based on comparing oxide scale characteristics across the three alloys, though the adhesion test (scratch/pull-off) on a thin oxide scale at room temperature may not fully represent high-temperature spallation behavior.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is highly useful as it provides a direct, comparative framework to isolate the effect of the X element on protective oxide formation, a central question for designing oxidation-resistant high-entropy alloys.
